brief: An FPV drone pit station: a two-storey workbench for a drone pilot, seen from the front. Along the back, a row of six cells two storeys tall: at each end a tower of drawers for spare parts, one drawer on each storey with its front facing the viewer, and between the towers four bins on the top storey, most of them divided, holding M3 screws, nuts and standoffs. In front of the back row, a covered deck one storey high as the work surface. Lay a work pad along the deck with a 5-inch quad on it, a multimeter and a hex driver set at the pad's free end, and the radio and the goggles on the deck beside the pad, one on each side. Put the deck nearest the default view and the back row farthest from it, and use look to check the view.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
